Fantastic professor, great scholar, hugely knowledgable. Very soft spoken, but knows his stuff in and out. THE GUY for 19th century Am Lit. Easy going classes with a lot of discussion, easy to fudge if you didn't do the reading, and a reasonably easy grader on reading journals and papers.

Really nice guy. Runs a good, discussion-based class.  Accepts everyone's opinions and does not have the attitude that his views are the only correct ones.  The last quiz/final exam was really hard and almost unfair, though.  Moderately tough grader.

Discussion-based classes. Does not impose his own interpretations on his students. Rather, he gets students to critically read and discuss the text. I had him for 2 courses and then as suff advisor. Overall, simply awesome prof.

All of the quizzes are based directly off of the homework, so if you can understand that, you'll do fine in her course.

I love weiwei. She is genuinely nice and loves when students come to her office hours.  If you try and do the homework assigned you will most likely get an A. Some of her quizes can be hard but she will scale or do a make-up if the entire class does poorly.

She does have a Chinese  accent.  However, she is genuinely interested in helping students, and knows the material very well.  The textbook she assigned is ancient, though, and she takes class attendance a little bit too personally.

review_highlights.comment:
Genuinely passionate about the course material. Would always offer help to students who are obviously struggling (whether its written on your face or in an email). Exams were tough but left you with a better understanding of the material afterwards. His feedback is a bit harsh but always accurate.

Always look for if Zoz is teaching a 3000+ course.

This guy is a pretty cool dude. If you've ever seen Despicable Me, he could be Gru's brother because he looks and sounds exactly the same.  I like him a lot because he explains all the concepts and problems and also has us doing a lot of practice problems, which is very helpful after being in Burnhams class. If he's your conference guy, thats great

Professor Zozulya gave good lectures and posted notes online. Expect a large lecture setting in this introductory level course. Homework was all online, assigned every few days, and fairly graded. Three exams were given, and the last two were very difficult for many students. Do not fall behind in this class, and seek help when needed!!

Professor Zozulya is a genius and knows a lot about what he teaches. Ask questions, but only good questions. If you don't read the book and read it carefully, don't expect him to help you and spoon feed you the material. One bad thing about him is that he expects all to have a high level of mathematical maturity somewhat unreasonably.

Friendly personality makes him very interesting to listen to and he always tries to use diagrams and examples to explain the concepts. You would still have to go read the textbook to understand the concept fully, but then again you wouldn't have bought it if you didn't want to use it.
